_doc: The language of each theme — words a person inside that world actually says. NOT a list of objects visible at the scene: that mistake is what produced boards whose rows were legal English and nothing more. A word earns its place here only if a player who knows the theme would nod at it. Filtered at build time to ENABLE1 + popular + 3..6 letters, so over-listing is harmless and under-listing is not.

_rnb90s_note: LOCKED. Three tiers, strongest first. A row earns its place by being something a fan RECOGNISES — an act, or a record — not by being a music-adjacent noun. Two earlier drafts failed: the first led with label/master/credit/royalties, which the cultural bench blocked as documentary grievance-talk that centres the business over the music and writes the women out of a decade they authored; the second led with craft nouns (hook, verse, belt, croon), which was true but generic — a row reading `sigh` tells a player nothing. Entries are cut unless the word literally appears in the act or title: `escape` is NOT Xscape and `level` is NOT LeVert, and both were inflating counts before they were caught. The `voice` tier is support only and may never be a board's reason to exist.
